beats.text: A sequence diagram shows the messages between participants, in time order, from top to bottom.
Each participant is a lifeline: a head box, with a dashed line going down.
While a participant is busy, a thin bar appears on its line: the execution, also called activation.
Messages are arrows between lifelines. Each one has a sender and a receiver.
Combined fragments are boxes with an operator in the corner.
alt: alternatives. If this, else that.
opt: an option. It happens, or nothing happens.
break: do this instead of the rest. In the login example, after more than three failed attempts, break ends the process.
And ref, an interaction use, calls another diagram, so big diagrams stay simple.
Finally, an X at the bottom of a lifeline is a destruction occurrence: that participant is gone.
